notes: Built the two-button breadboard circuit with a common ground rail; the 2-leg and single 4-leg diagrams are variants of the same wiring and were not built separately.

Breadboard image 'rows' 5, 7, 10, 12 are column numbers in the catalogue naming. Buttons straddle the centre gap (top-half row e and bottom-half row f). The jumper wires go in row a of the same column, which is the same strip as the button's e leg.
Ground rail is modelled as the 'tn' rail. The exact hole index along the rail is not significant because the rail is one strip (tn.1, tn.6, tn.10 used).

Each button's ground side is column 5 (button 1) or column 10 (button 2), wired to the ground rail. The signal side is column 7 (GPIO17) or column 12 (GPIO5). The Pi's GND wire goes to physical pin 6, GND.1, next to GP3.
GPIO17 is the manual's stated input pin; GPIO5 is the second button's input as shown in the image.
